title: I'lam al-Muwaqqi'in 'an Rabb al-'Alamin
author: ibn-qayyim
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya's long work on giving legal opinions: who may speak for God in the law, the sources of Ahmad ibn Hanbal's fatwas, the limits of analogy, a sustained critique of blind imitation, the wisdom behind rulings and the changing of fatwas with time and place.
historicalContext: Ibn Qayyim was Ibn Taymiyya's leading student in Damascus. The I'lam, built around a commentary on 'Umar's letter on judging, is one of the classic statements of the case for independent legal reasoning.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
